Choosing questions for your survey

Source: vignettes/articles/learn/question-types.Rmd
question-types.Rmd

Choose a question type to match the information you need, from agreement ratings and dates to written feedback and ranked options. Each type below links to a page that shows how to add it. The input_types demo holds all 13: open it from RStudio’s Addins menu with surveyframe: Try a demo.

Questions, response options and scales

A question asks 1 thing. Its response options are the labelled choices it offers, such as Strongly disagree to Strongly agree, and related questions can share 1 set of options. A scored scale combines a group of related questions into 1 score, such as an organisation score from 4 agreement questions, and its reliability is checked as a whole. Add a Likert question to a scale shows the steps.

The 13 question types

Type What the respondent does Suits
Likert Rates agreement on a labelled scale Scored scales, reliability, ordinal tests
Single choice Picks 1 option Frequencies, cross-tabulations, group comparisons
Multiple choice Picks any options Frequencies, Cochran’s Q
Numeric Types a number Descriptives, t-tests, regression
Short text Types a line Text analysis
Long text Types a paragraph Text analysis, topic models
Date Picks a date Descriptives
Grid (matrix) Rates a set of rows on 1 scale Descriptives, scored scales
Slider Drags to a value Descriptives, correlation
Ranking Orders options Rank descriptives
Star rating Gives stars Descriptives, ordinal tests
Pairwise comparison Judges which of 2 criteria matters more (Saaty), or how much 1 influences another (0 to 4) AHP, ANP, DEMATEL
Criteria weights Divides 100 points across criteria Decision methods

The 2 layout elements are a section break, which starts a new page with a heading, and a text block, which shows text and collects no answer.

Any question can be required, shown only when an earlier answer allows it (branching), or checked for attention (attention checks).

For analysis: how answers are stored

Each type stores its answer in a declared shape, so the analysis plan matches each method to the answers it can use. Likert, single choice, slider, star rating and numeric questions store 1 value. A multiple choice question stores 1 column per option, a grid 1 column per row, a pairwise comparison 1 column per pair compared, and criteria weights 1 column per criterion. Text and date questions store the text or date given, and a ranking stores the order.
